content:
The test image shows soybean **leaves** with:
- Yellow-green mottling/mosaic pattern
- Dark brown lesions with reddish-brown borders
- Some tissue holes where dead tissue may have fallen out

This narrows to the 16 leaf classes. Top candidates based on symptoms: Sudden_death_syndrome, Downy_mildew, Frogeye_leaf_spot, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Septoria_brown_spot, Bacterial_Blight, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Cercospora.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.

SDS shows severe interveinal necrosis with green veins remaining - much more advanced than the test image. The test image has a more mottled, patchy yellow-green pattern with scattered discrete lesions. Not a strong match.
Downy mildew shows small discrete yellow spots - the test image has more diffuse mottling plus brown lesions. Not a great match.
SVN shows localized yellow/brown spots along veins - the test image has much more extensive, diffuse mottling. Not matching well.

Frogeye leaf spot shows small discrete spots with gray centers and reddish-brown borders on otherwise green leaves - no mottling. Not matching the test image's extensive mottling pattern.

Let me check Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus - the "green to yellow mottling" description matches well.

BPMV shows puckering and mottling but the test image also has distinct brown lesions with reddish-brown borders that BPMV doesn't typically show. Partial match on mottling.

Let me check Bacterial_Blight and Septoria_brown_spot.
Bacterial blight shows angular yellow/brown spots but not the diffuse mottling of the test image. Let me check Septoria brown spot.
Septoria shows overall yellowing with small dark spots - different from the test image's mottled green-yellow pattern with larger bordered lesions. Let me check Cercospora with my last view.

This Cercospora reference is a strong match. It shows the same pattern as the test image:
- Yellow-green mottling/discoloration across the leaf
- Reddish-brown spots scattered throughout
- Holes where necrotic tissue has fallen out
- Overall "sunburned" leathery appearance

The Cercospora description matches well: "Light purple spots on upper leaf surfaces that expand to reddish-purple or bronze discoloration, giving a leathery sunburned appearance" with "red-brown spots on both leaf surfaces that coalesce into large necrotic areas."

The symptom description of light purple spots expanding to reddish-purple or bronze discoloration with a leathery sunburned appearance fits well. Other candidates (SDS, Downy mildew, BPMV, Frogeye, Bacterial blight, SVN, Septoria) showed distinctly different lesion patterns."}
